summary: Edge proxy buffer flush race causing intermittent 502/503 wave under tenant burst
description:
Issue summary:
Edge proxy instances serving tenant brighthealth experienced a synchronized 502/503 wave during a planned marketing-driven traffic burst. Errors started as transient connection resets but escalated into sustained 502s for ~22 minutes before partial mitigation.

Impact:
- Multiple BrightHealth.ai endpoints returned 502/503 for ~10-40% of requests during the peak window (approx 11:02-11:24 UTC).
- Streaming sessions frequently dropped mid-response; some non-streaming calls retried by client and hit quota limits.
- Customer reported degraded user experience and several timed-out callbacks.

Environment:
- Production (prod), us-east region.
- Tenant: BrightHealth.ai (dedicated cluster).

Observed behavior:
- Sequence of events shows sharp increase in edge-proxy memory RSS followed by periodic buffer flush failures on the proxy layer, triggering upstream connection resets and 502s emitted from api-gateway.
- Autoscaler kicked in for serving-runtime but initial proxy failures prevented healthy handoff for a subset of requests.

Expected behavior:
- Edge proxy should gracefully handle buffer flushes and backpressure without creating coordinated connection resets across workers. Autoscaler should absorb burst without increasing 5xx surface.

Relevant logs/metrics (high level):
- edge-proxy logs: repeated "buffer flush failed: write: connection reset by peer" across Nginx worker processes; spool growth observed.
- api-gateway: 502 spike aligned with proxy error spikes; upstream response latency increased from 45ms to 1.2s at peak.
- runtime metrics: KV cache thrash rate increased by 3x during burst window.
- heap/RSS on edge-proxy containers climbed from 290MB -> 1.8GB over ~4m before OOM killer incidents on one replica.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Simulated tenant burst using our loadgen (tenant credentials for BrightHealth.ai) to replay customer traffic profile (mix of streaming + short text generation).
2) Ramp from baseline 120 RPS to 2k RPS over 90s with streaming sessions making up ~40% of concurrent requests.
3) Observe proxy and api-gateway metrics; reproduce buffer flush error pattern and 502 wave within ~2-4 minutes of ramp.

Temporary workaround provided to customer:
- Rate-limited incoming tenant traffic at the ingress layer to reduce peak concurrency.
- Switched tenant routing to alternate edge-proxy pool in a different AZ which reduced error rate.

Next steps requested:
- Deep SRE review of edge-proxy buffer and flush codepath and any library upgrades.
- Add additional guardrails on proxy to avoid coordinated buffer spiking across replicas.
- Evaluate fast-fail strategy upstream to avoid retry amplification.
steps_to_reproduce: Use internal loadgen with BrightHealth.ai tenant profile
Ramp from 120 RPS to 2000 RPS over 90 seconds with ~40% streaming sessions
Monitor edge-proxy logs and api-gateway 5xx metrics; expect buffer flush errors within 2-4 minutes

[api-gateway] 2026-03-11T11:02:20Z WARN upstream returned 502 for request id=req_xx7a3

comments: Support (Aisha): Customer reported sudden increase in 502s starting ~11:02 UTC, provided logs and request IDs. Opened ticket and escalated to SRE.
SRE (Diego): Initial triage shows edge-proxy RSS spike followed by buffer flush failures. Spun up alternate pool to stabilize traffic as temporary mitigation.
Customer (BrightHealth.ai - Raj Patel): Confirmed alternate pool reduced 5xx rate to baseline; still seeking root cause and ETA for full fix.
Eng (Mina Chen): Noted similar guardrail changes were proposed in PR #4321 but not yet rolled out cluster-wide. Will validate patch applicability to Nginx/Go proxy code.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: coordinated buffer growth caused by streaming payload retention during brief network stalls leading to simultaneous flush attempts.
Hypothesis 2: a regression in proxy library upgrade (libproto v2.4.0) that changed non-blocking write semantics under high concurrency.
Evidence: memory RSS jumps precede connection resets; one proxy replica hit OOM and was restarted by k8s during window.
Action taken: reproduced locally with loadgen; confirmed buffer flush errors at similar RPS/streaming ratio; created repo PR to add exponential jitter to flush timers.
Action taken: temporarily adjusted autoscaler thresholds to pre-warm additional runtime instances earlier during tenant bursts.
resolution: Mitigation applied: tenant rerouted to alternate edge pool and ingress rate limiting enabled. Immediate 5xx amplitude reduced to <2% for BrightHealth.ai. Long-term fix workstream opened: patch proxy flush jitter and add per-replica flush backoff. Targeting staged rollout next week after QA. Follow-up action: add targeted e2e test in loadgen for mixed streaming bursts.
